title: Priority inversion in reserved capacity allocator causing tenant denial during elasticity spikes
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
During a regional elasticity spike (high short-lived QPS from several customers) the reserved-capacity allocator entered a priority inversion state where small/medium tenants were repeatedly denied burst allocations while large tenants consumed replenished headroom. The allocator comparator relied on a single 'last_allocated' metric; under concurrent refill and preemptive-eviction races this produced deterministic ordering that favored long-running heavy tenants and systematically starved smaller tenants until their burst credits were exhausted.

Why this is unique / root cause hypothesis:
- The allocator used a deterministic sort key (last_allocated timestamp) with no tie-break based on tenant weight or remaining headroom, producing a priority inversion under contention.
- Refill loop and eviction loop were both retrying without jitter; simultaneous retries caused the same tenant set to repeatedly win allocation windows.
- Lease reconciliation logic was eventually-consistent and allowed stale leases to be re-granted for already-drained slots due to a window where token tombstones weren't observed.
- KV cache pinning (local to the serving shard) kept slots occupied during rapid backfills, increasing effective occupancy and reducing visible headroom to the allocator.

Impact observed:
- Multiple customers (support tickets opened by three mid-market customers) experienced sustained 30-90s request queuing and burst-denials during peak minutes.
- Observed metrics: reserved_pool_success_rate dropped 15pp for the affected AZ; headroom_utilization spiked to 98% despite autoscaler signals indicating available capacity. Latency SLOs were missed for affected tenants for ~18 minutes at first detection.

Immediate mitigations applied (hotfix runbook):
1) Emergency rollback of deterministic ordering: toggled allocator.feature.priority_jitter=true via runtime flag to introduce randomized tie-breaks (rolled out in 2 AZs within 6m).
2) Throttle cap added at admission: per-tenant micro-slice reservation of 2% headroom for small-tenants (config override tenant_selector=small-tenants) to prevent full hogging.
3) Lease reconciliation tightened: reduced lease_tombstone_ttl from 30s -> 5s to shorten re-grant window.
4) KV cache soft-eviction enabled for backfill windows to free pinned slots for 60s_backfill_period.
These mitigations restored fairness within ~12 minutes and reduced customer-visible denials.

Permanent fix plan:
- Short-term (this sprint): update allocator comparator to be multi-dimensional: (1) tenant_weight, (2) remaining_burst_headroom, (3) last_allocated timestamp with minimal jitter. Add unit and integration tests for race scenarios.
- Mid-term: introduce an admission micro-slicing policy and a weighted reservoir allocator that guarantees minimum slices per tenant class under contention. Provide a config-driven floor for micro-slices.
- Long-term: instrument and expose a deterministic fairness dashboard (per-tenant allocation traces) and add an anomaly detector on priority inversion signals (rapid re-ordering + repeated wins).

Testing and validation:
- Created synthetic load harness that reproduces priority inversion by driving concurrent refill+eviction loops (see harness entrypoint: tools/allocator/sim/priority_inversion_test.go).
- Added concurrency fuzz tests to allocator core with >10k runs to validate comparator stability across races.
- Integration smoke in staging with mixed-tenancy traffic profile A/B (jad:staging-allocator-a, jad:staging-allocator-b).

Rollback and rollout plan:
- Fix PR will be staged to canary in two AZs for 24h. Canary gating: no tenant denial spikes, headroom_utilization < 90%, and no negative impact to warmup latency.
- Progressive rollout to remaining AZs over 4 hours with pausing on anomaly.

Customer comms and follow-up:
- Initial on-call comms sent to affected customers with temporary mitigations and ETA for permanent fix. Support ticket links: https://support.redwood.ai/ticket/RED-7801, RED-7804, RED-7810.
- Postmortem and technical writeup scheduled into Cycle 11. Customer-facing summary to be prepared by Customer Success once permanent fix is live.

Artifacts and links:
- Repro harness: github.com/redwood-inference/allocator-sim/tree/main/priority_inversion_test.go
- Hotfix PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6821
- Proposed fix PR (WIP): github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6880
- Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/alloc/fairness-overview

Acceptance criteria for closure:
1) No recurrence in canary or prod for 7 days under similar spike patterns.
2) Integration tests and fuzz harness merged in main.
3) Postmortem published with timeline and customer communications attached.
4) Config knobs documented in ops runbook and Console (micro-slice floor adjustable).

Notes for implementers:
- Be cautious changing the comparator: small differences cause large allocation patterns; include deterministic seeding options for testing.
- Avoid introducing latency in hot path: comparator must remain O(1) and cheap — precompute keys where possible.
